A desktop app for Git branches and GitHub pull requests. Comment on any line, publish when you're ready, and add an AI reviewer with your own model, or none. Since AI started writing so much of our code, reviewing it all has become the hardest part of my job. So I built Review: a desktop app for reviewing pull requests, where you can set up a team of AI reviewers from different providers to take the first pass. - Opens your local Git branches and GitHub pull requests in one window. - Keeps your comments on your machine until you publish them to GitHub as a review. **What's different about the AI part**: it checks every change against a fixed set of rules (bugs, security, error handling, tests and more), and it shows which rules it actually checked, not just what it found. If a request fails, you can retry only the rules it missed. One heads-up: the installers aren't signed yet, so your system will ask once the first time you open it. I'd love to know: what's the most annoying part of code review for you today? No reviews yet Be the first to leave a review for Review Leave a review.
